items.title: Crude oil prices may fall to $75 by December as West Asia tensions ease
points: “If West Asian tensions continue to cool, crude may move towards USD 75 per barrel by December 2026.
In this supportive scenario, equities could scale new highs, while the rupee may strengthen towards 90 per US dollar,” SP Sharma, Chief Economist, ASSOCHAM, told ANI.
Sharma said West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil was currently trading at around USD 87 per barrel in the global market.
According to Sharma, improving prospects for peace in West Asia, supported by developments involving the United States, had strengthened hopes of easing geopolitical risks.

Meanwhile, Ajay Srivastava, Founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), attributed the recent decline in crude oil prices to geopolitical developments that have eased fears of fresh strikes on Iran.
According to the GTRI analysis, Brent crude fell to USD 90 per barrel on November 10, down around 24 per cent from its October 30 level of USD 118 per barrel.

items.title: Hebbal Short tunnel project threatens green corridor supporting 199 bird species: Study
points: The report was prepared by Harini Nagendra, Seema Mundoli, Prachi Gupta, and Vivek G. of Azim Premji University, Bengaluru.

items.title: BIS seizes 16 water coolers without ISI mark in Malappuram
points: The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) seized 16 drinking water coolers without the mandatory ISI mark during a search at a unit at Melmuri, Malappuram, on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).
A team of officials from the BIS Kochi office conducted the inspection to check compliance with the Self-Contained Drinking Water Cooler (Quality Control) Order, 2023.
The seized coolers included one with a storage capacity of 45 litres and 15 others with capacities ranging from 15 to 50 litres.
Manufacturing, stocking, selling, or distributing drinking water coolers without the mandatory BIS standard mark violates Section 17 of the BIS Act, 2016, read with the 2023 Quality Control Order.
The search and seizure were carried out under Section 28 of the BIS Act.
The BIS advised consumers to verify the authenticity of certified products through the BIS Care mobile app by checking their registration numbers (R-Numbers).
Consumers can also report the misuse of the ISI mark, CRS mark, or BIS hallmark through the app.

items.title: TGCSB flags rise in fake shopping ads, card frauds
points: The bureau said it had recorded a sharp increase in complaints involving two types of fraud over the past 20 to 30 days.
After attracting customers, they collect advance payments through UPI, digital wallets or bank transfers and send fake order confirmations.
They then cite delivery delays before blocking the customers’ numbers and shutting down their websites without delivering the products or services.

items.title: Despite Ban, Pak's Toxic Fairness Cream Sold In Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh
points: India has stopped trade with Pakistan but even so, a fairness cream smuggled from across the border has flooded the market.
Despite warnings about its high-risk contents, its sale continues unabated in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and several other parts of the country.
The Goree Beauty Cream -- priced between Rs 380 and Rs 800 -- is sold in markets and is also available across all online platforms.
The cream has 5,000 ppm (parts per million) of mercury, whereas the level should be less than 1 ppm.
Maharashtra has banned the cream after its doctors pieced together the story when they found 18 women suffering from severe kidney damage.

items.title: Multi-agency coastal defence exercise 'Sea Vigil-26' begins
points: Mumbai, 'Sea Vigil-26', the fifth edition of a pan-India coastal defence exercise, began on Wednesday, officials said.
It involves 21 agencies across six ministries and is being coordinated by the Indian Navy as lead agency, a Defence release said.
The exercise is being conducted in two phases: The Coastal Defence and Security Readiness Evaluation phase from November 11 to 17, followed by the Sea Phase on November 18 and 19.
Exercise Sea Vigil was conceptualised in 2018 to validate the measures instituted to strengthen maritime security in the aftermath of the 26/11 Mumbai terror attacks.

Sea Vigil-26 will span the entire coastline and Exclusive Economic Zone of India, and involve all coastal states and union territories along with other maritime stakeholders including the fishing and coastal communities, the statement said.

The conduct of the exercise is being facilitated by the Ministries of Defence; Home Affairs; Ports, Shipping and Waterways; Petroleum and Natural Gas; and Fisheries, and Animal Husbandry and Dairying.
